chapter: Chicago pianists and New Orleans bands
title: The Elite clubs on State Street and Tony Jackson's funeral
summary: Addresses of Elite No. 1 and No. 2, the cafe bands there, and Tony Jackson as the featured star.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: The boys at the Elite, yes. The Elite band.
Where was the Elite number one? What street? 3030 State Street. 3030?
Yes. And the number two, where was that? 3445 State Street.
Is that building? Is that building?
No, it's all down. It's all down. It's all down. They've played all those things up there.
I think I took a picture a few years ago of the number two. I never did see the number one.
Yeah, number two was right front. Tina and John.
Yes, that's where Tony makes it a lot.
Did they have a band there too or just piano?

Just a cafe band. A combination of lines. Carnet, you'd see a Carnet tonight maybe with him. Or Trumon tomorrow night you'd go and see a band or something else. Because Tony was featured. He was a star. I played at Tony's funeral.
Yes. And Charlie Young sang. A fellow from St. Louis.
